content: CONFIRMED — `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage4-host-restart.mjs` spawns `cmd.exe /c .\gradlew.bat` on Windows (lines 22–30), but fallback cleanup invokes only `host.kill()` (lines 95–102). `running(host)` inspects only that `cmd.exe` ChildProcess’s `exitCode` and `signalCode` (lines 302–304), not descendants. A local Node v24.20.0 Windows probe using the same `cmd.exe /c <long-lived child>` topology showed the wrapper exited with `SIGTERM` and `running=false` while its descendant remained alive. Since `gradlew.bat` launches Java and Gradle’s `JavaExec` launches the fixture JVM, fallback cleanup can consider the host stopped while Java descendants survive. The normal `STOP` path exits cooperatively; this affects fallback termination.
